marks.gloss_en: מנא אמינא לה? the mishna: extended its foreleg and did not draw it back -- invalid. When? if at the end of slaughter, would it go on living? rather, in the middle
the convulsion must come in the middle of the slaughter (not at its start)
אמר ליה רבא: לעולם at the end -- any that does not do so at the end, its soul evidently departed before
the convulsion must come at the very end of the slaughter
מנא אמינא לה? R' Shimon's mishna -- walls full of blood, valid -- and Shmuel: the walls of the slaughter-cut. Fine if [the sign] is at the start; if at the end, perhaps it spurted at the start
דתנן, אמר רבי שמעון: השוחט בלילה ולמחר מצא כתלים מלאים דם -- כשרה, שזינקה
Shmuel: [the mishna's 'walls'] -- we learned the walls of the slaughter-cut
ודלמא שאני זינוק, דעדיף -- perhaps spurting is different, being superior
תנינא: בהמה דקה שפשטה ידה ולא החזירה -- פסולה; הא החזירה -- כשרה
[from the mishna:] but if it drew [the leg] back -- valid
מיתיבי: R' Meir -- lowing at slaughter is not convulsion; and in his name, even excreting or tail-wagging is not -- קשיא גועה אגועה, קשיא ריעי אריעי
the baraita: R' Yosei said, R' Meir used to say: lowing at the time of slaughter is not convulsion
גועה אגועה לא קשיא: this one where its voice is thick, that one where its voice is thin
ריעי אריעי נמי לא קשיא: here where it flows, there where it spurts
ומדרבנן מי עדיף? והא תנן: וחכמים אומרים עד שתפרכס -- the Rabbis answer R' Eliezer (not R' Gamliel, else 'once it convulsed'), and if spurting were superior, what is 'until'? (left unanswered)
Rav (per his students, answering Shmuel's 'what did Rav say about the dying animal?'): if it lowed, excreted, or twitched its ear -- that is convulsion
Shmuel (as Rav Anan reports): if its leg was bent and it extended it -- that is a thing a dead animal does
Rav Chisda: the convulsion they spoke of is at the end of the slaughter
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: the convulsion they spoke of is at the start of the slaughter
[R' Eliezer's] spurting is lighter than R' Gamliel's [measure] and superior to the Rabbis'
Avuha deBar Avuvram: the Rabbis are responding to R' Eliezer (were it R' Gamliel they would have said 'once it convulsed'); and if [spurting] were superior, what is 'until'?
